text:
A fire outbreak on Saturday engulfed parts of the Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria (FRCN), Kaduna Zonal Station, while some senior staff were undergoing promotion interview.
The cause of the fire, which started in the afternoon, was yet to be established as of the time of filing this report.
The fire affected the studios of Karama FM, newly renovated Supreme FM and parts of the Hausa Service section of the station.
Daily Trust gathered that some senior staff from the North West and other Zonal offices were at the station for the promotion interview when the incident occurred.
Fire service personnel were seen battling the inferno to contain it and prevent it from spreading to other sections of the station.
The station also announced the incident on its verified Facebook page.
“Some of the senior staff were undergoing promotion interviews at the premises when we saw smoke coming out of the Karama FM and newly renovated Supreme FM sections.
“I cannot say whether it affected the Hausa Service section, but that area was also covered with smoke,” a staff member said.
Another staff member confirmed the incident, saying the Director-General of the corporation, Mohammed Bulama, was also at the station when the fire broke out.
The unamed staff described the incident as worrisome, noting that the station was already facing some challenges and expressed hope that urgent measures would be taken to repair the damage.
“The supreme FM was newly renovated by the management and other sections too are underway to be renovated before this fire incident. With this fire incident we don’t know how long it will take the station to bounce back,” he said.
When contacted by telephone, the Acting Zonal Director of the station, Aminu Abdullahi, declined to comment, saying fire service personnel were still working to contain the inferno.
FRCN, founded in 1962 by the late Sir Ahmadu Bello, the Sardauna of Sokoto and Premier of the Northern Region, Radio Nigeria Kaduna has served audiences across Northern Nigeria and beyond for decades.
The station, which became a federal establishment following the merger of the Nigeria Broadcasting Corporation and the Broadcasting Corporation of Northern Nigeria in 1978, is one of the country’s longstanding broadcasting institutions.
The Kaduna Zonal Station operates several services, including the Hausa Service, Karama FM and Supreme FM, with programmes covering news, education, culture and public affairs.
It also oversees Radio Nigeria stations across several states in the North-West region.
